approach.method_basis: The reference is Genetic GFN, published by Kim and colleagues, a two-phase generator that keeps handing work between a learned sampler and ordinary graph editing. A sequence model that writes molecules one token at a time is first trained on a large unlabeled corpus of drug-like structures, then adapted separately for each objective so that the chance of it finishing any particular molecule rises with the score that molecule actually received. Molecules it samples are dropped into a small scored population, which is then improved by ordinary genetic operations on the molecular graph: crossover between two parents, and single atom, bond and ring edits. The scored offspring are turned back into training targets for the sequence model, drawn preferentially from the high-scoring end of the archive, so the network proposes globally, the graph operators refine locally, and the refined results reshape what the network proposes next. A learned scaling term lets the model fit that reward-proportional target without knowing the total reward in advance, and a pull back toward the frozen corpus-trained model keeps it from collapsing onto whatever it found first.
approach.novelty: This is a root, so everything concrete here is a choice the implementation makes rather than something inherited from a parent. It fixes the alternation as one neural batch followed by two graph batches of ten molecules each, so roughly two thirds of the evaluation budget goes to graph refinement rather than to the network. It forces neural output into the breeding population at every cycle boundary instead of letting the population close over itself. It caps the scored population at sixty-four members. It sets the training reward as an exponential in the raw score, so a small score difference becomes a large difference in training weight. It draws replay targets with a probability that falls off as one over rank, so top molecules are revisited without the rest of the archive being starved. And it trains the corpus model only on unlabeled data, keeping every reward-bearing update local to one objective, so nothing learned from one objective can leak into another.

observed_bottleneck: This root has no Parent. The benchmark requires task-local discoveries to become useful proposals again before scarce feedback is exhausted. Observation n-4fa9546e559e confirms valid graph evolution, improving offspring and survivor reuse, while most evaluated descendants did not exceed their best generating parent. This motivates propagating useful graph discoveries through a learned global proposal distribution, but does not establish that the reciprocal Genetic GFN cycle improves on graph evolution or that the hybrid needs surrogate guidance. The root must establish that both directions of the graph-to-policy-to-population cycle occur quickly enough to matter.
hypothesis: Alternate de novo sampling from a task-local GFlowNet SMILES policy with graph crossover and mutation of its refreshed scored population, then distill accepted graph descendants back into the policy through rank-weighted off-policy trajectory-balance replay with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen corpus-trained prior.

finding_summary.headline: Best of the thirteen Discovery roots at 0.5103, but the lead rests on one near-saturated objective
finding_summary.insights: The reciprocal loop demonstrably ran, and the node running it leads a field of thirteen roots whose scores span 0.2331 to 0.5103. What the run does not show is that the coupling produced the lead. Most graph offspring still fell below their generating parent, which is exactly the limitation this lineage was framed to address, so the advantage may come from the corpus-trained prior supplying realistic starting chemistry rather than from the feedback cycle itself. The per-objective spread is the sharper message: the same optimizer that nearly saturates one objective returns roughly 0.20 on another, so the campaign's current ranking is driven mostly by how well a method's proposal distribution happens to overlap each objective's answer, not by uniform competence, and a macro mean over five objectives will reward a method that wins one of them outright. With one seed and no parent this is not a reliability claim. What stays open is whether the lead survives more seeds, and whether being selective about which descendants get evaluated would convert the four-fifths of offspring that currently degrade their parent into usable gains.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.510250764298028 on the single screening seed, the highest of the thirteen roots. Per objective the run returned 0.989650581855642 on the docking objective, 0.6290937996820349 on the decoration objective, then 0.46331566856387824, 0.27137962936984883 and 0.19781414201873615 on the remaining three, so one near-saturated result plus one strong result carry most of the lead while three objectives sit low. Every pre-registered observable activated and the falsifier did not trigger. The corpus-only prior cut held-out token loss from 4.560865074576297 to 0.5625432162352548 over 29742 steps on 1268755 sequences, and 150 later integrity checks found zero changes to it. Five hundred policy-generated molecules were admitted across 50 population refreshes, and 2958 complete graph-to-policy-to-sample-to-breeding chains were reconstructed through 106 distinct policy bridges. All 76800 replay draws came from accepted observations, with realized top-rank enrichment 0.2551173919195906 above the 0.5 uniform reference. Trajectory-balance residual fell from 27.86439877950252 to 22.643096844616046 across 2400 updates, 2381 of which reduced it, and all 2240 graph-bearing updates produced nonzero graph-derived gradients over 54110 draws. Of 1450 unique proposals, 500 came from the policy and 950 from graph operators, but only 173 descendants (18.2 percent) strictly beat their best generating parent, and the mean child-minus-best-parent change was -0.09497708681416797.

molecular.headline: Real medicinal chemistry with hard per-objective motif lock-in, and not one defined stereocentre
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the generator emits ring-rich, heavily aromatic, well-branched molecules of ordinary size: ring closure appears in 95 to 99 percent of proposals, aromatic atoms in 87 to 97 percent, mean SMILES length runs 43 to 59, and cumulated double bonds are essentially absent at under one percent. The chemistry is recognisably drawn from a drug-like corpus, with indoles, pyridines, oxazoles, methoxyaryls, amides and benzylamines recurring. Two things are uniformly missing. No proposal in any objective carries a defined stereocentre. And within each objective the top of the ranking collapses onto a single decorated scaffold that is then permuted one atom at a time, so the twelve best molecules are usually variants of one structure rather than twelve independent answers.

per_task.generated_character: Genuine dopaminergic pharmacophore. A tryptamine-like indole carrying a primary or secondary amine, joined through a single methylene to a brominated tetrahydroisoquinoline. These are molecules a medicinal chemist would recognise on sight, and they reach 0.989650581855642 from starting material at 0.019.
liabilities: heavy reliance on aryl bromide, which reads as a synthetic handle rather than a finished substituent
aminal-like N-CH2-N fragments appearing in several of the top-scoring entries
the single best entry stacks two bromides on one ring plus a fused diazepane, an unusually greasy strained core
missing_features: defined stereochemistry at the ring-fusion and benzylic centres these scaffolds genuinely possess
conformationally constrained linkers other than the single methylene bridge used everywhere
aryl substitution beyond bromide and chloride on the tetrahydroisoquinoline ring
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks one triad: free basic amine, indole, and a halogenated benzylamine partner. Everything above 0.97 has all three; the bottom of the trajectory is amine-free heteroaryl chemistry such as triazine ethers and thiourea-adjacent amides, scoring four orders of magnitude lower.

per_task.generated_character: One motif, repeated. A 1,3-oxazol-5-yl group hung off an aminopyridine that is fused or linked to a lactone or lactam ring, with a second oxazole carried on an exocyclic alkene. Eleven of the twelve best entries are one- or two-atom permutations of each other.
liabilities: hemiaminal and enol fragments written NC(O)=C, which are tautomer artefacts rather than isolable species
an exocyclic C(=C) alkene conjugated to a ring carbonyl in nearly every top molecule, a Michael acceptor
trivial fragments such as CC and CCCN entering the trajectory at all, which wastes evaluations
missing_features: saturated or partly saturated ring systems to break the flat all-heteroaryl character
any defined stereocentre, despite several sp3 ring-fusion carbons being present
substituent chemistry beyond methyl, isopropyl and anilino on the central pyridine
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The scoring band is extremely compressed: best 0.6290937996820349 against a starting set already at 0.5, and everything above 0.62 carries the paired-oxazole plus aminopyridine arrangement. The worst entries are either oversized sulfone and bisphosphonate adducts or trivial fragments that still score exactly 0.5, so the objective floors small molecules rather than punishing them.

per_task.generated_character: Two families sharing one tail. A clean one, a methoxyphenyl ether of a pyridine carboxamide with a picolylamide cap, which is ordinary amide chemistry. And a dominant one built around an acryl-aldehyde enol ether, O=CC=C(O-aryl), capped by a non-aromatic 2H-pyrrole ring.
liabilities: O=CC=C(O-aryl) is a conjugated aldehyde and a Michael acceptor, and it is in most of the top twelve
C1C=CC=N1 2H-pyrrole rings are tautomerically unstable and not isolable as drawn
N=C(S) thioimidate and OOC peroxy-methyl fragments appear in mid-ranked entries
missing_features: a stable connectivity that reproduces what the acryl-aldehyde enol ether is contributing
aromatic five-membered rings in place of the non-aromatic 2H-pyrroles the generator keeps emitting
defined stereochemistry at the sp3 ring carbons of the pyrrolines it builds
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 2-pyridylmethyl group is the recurring feature of everything above 0.37. The stable amide family and the reactive enol-ether family reach almost the same score, so the objective is not discriminating between them. The very bottom is occupied both by fragments and by overlong multi-ring adducts, both scoring effectively zero, so size is punished at both ends.

per_task.generated_character: A single scaffold explored exhaustively. A 1,3-dimethyl hydantoin-dione ring joined by an exocyclic double bond to a benzylic carbon that also carries a phenyl and an alkyl-aryl ether. All twelve best entries are that same molecule with the alkyl decoration and ring size varied.
liabilities: the exocyclic alkene sits between two ring carbonyls, making it a strong Michael acceptor in every top entry
late proposals introduce an O-O peroxy linkage and an N-hydroxy hydantoin, both degradation-prone
one late proposal carries a fully conjugated triene tail, which is not a stable substituent
missing_features: a second distinct scaffold family, to test whether the plateau is the objective's ceiling or the search's
polar functionality on the phenoxy ring beyond a single hydroxyl
defined stereochemistry at the benzylic and hydantoin sp3 centres
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Scores are banded between 0.184 and 0.198 for the whole top twelve, and the only gradient is small alkyl decoration: adding an ethyl or propyl on the phenoxy ring, or fusing a cyclobutane onto it, moves the score by thousandths. The floor is trivial fragments, so the objective rewards mere presence of the motif far more than any refinement of it.

per_task.generated_character: Nitro-substituted cyclohexadiene rings carrying a pyridin-2-ylmethyl hydrazone. The charged-fragment rate here is 0.3655, far above the 0.01 to 0.03 seen on the other objectives, and that charge is almost entirely the nitro group the generator has latched onto.
liabilities: malformed nitro groups written [N+][O-] without the second oxygen appear inside the top twelve
hydrazones are hydrolytically labile and are the single load-bearing feature of the whole top set
nitroalkene fragments, both reactive and toxicophoric, recur across the highest-scoring molecules
missing_features: the fluorinated aryl and fused triazole chemistry a chemist would reach for on this kind of target
any defined stereocentre, though this objective family is built around configuration
aromatic carbocycles in place of the non-aromatic cyclohexadiene rings that dominate the top set
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Every entry above 0.19 pairs a hydrazone C=NN with a 2-pyridyl or picolyl group, with the nitro group added on top. The worst molecules are large polyfunctional adducts scoring down to 1e-87, so this objective punishes size ferociously and the search responded by shrinking rather than by getting the chemistry right.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 in all five trajectory sets, across 1450 proposals, even though the molecules routinely contain sp3 ring-fusion and benzylic carbons that are genuine stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never emits a defined stereocentre.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Configuration is outside the proposal alphabet as built. A generator aimed at shape-dependent properties would need stereo tags in its token vocabulary and stereo-aware graph edits, plus feedback able to distinguish two configurations of the same skeleton, otherwise half of the accessible chemistry is unreachable by construction.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In every trajectory the twelve best molecules are one- or two-atom permutations of the same core, the winning family is reached early and then only decorated, and the score spread across those twelve is often under 0.02.
transferable_gaps.gap: Within any one objective the search collapses onto a single decorated scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Reward-weighted replay concentrates the proposal distribution faster than local graph edits can leave it. A generator would need something that explicitly keeps distinct cores alive, such as similarity-penalised replay or budget reserved for proposals sampled far from the current archive, rather than relying on random atom edits to escape a basin they helped dig.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Conjugated aldehyde enol ethers, exocyclic alkenes flanked by ring carbonyls, hemiaminal NC(O)=C fragments, 2H-pyrroles and nitro groups written with only one oxygen all appear in the top-scoring sets, not merely in the discarded tail.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive electrophiles and tautomer artefacts are proposed as if they were finished molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Nothing in the loop distinguishes a scoreable string from a makeable compound, so a reactive motif that happens to score can become the load-bearing feature of the archive and then be amplified by replay. A structural-alert and valence-sanity screen applied before a proposal spends an evaluation would stop that amplification.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Only 173 of 950 graph descendants strictly beat their best generating parent, an 18.2 percent rate, and the mean child-minus-best-parent score change across the run was -0.09497708681416797.
transferable_gaps.gap: Local graph edits usually make their parent worse.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Descendants are being evaluated indiscriminately, so four fifths of the graph budget buys degradation. A generator would gain from a cheap internal ranking over candidate descendants before real evaluations are spent, so the budget goes to the offspring most likely to exceed the parent they came from.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The aromatic-atom rate runs 0.87 to 0.97 across every set, the recurring rings are five- and six-membered heteroaromatics, and the few sp3 rings present are small carbocycles bolted on as peripheral substituents.
transferable_gaps.gap: Saturated three-dimensional ring systems are almost absent.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The proposal distribution has inherited the flat, heteroaryl-dense character of its pretraining corpus. A generator would need edit operations that build and fuse saturated rings, and a prior whose sampling does not collapse onto planar aromatic frameworks, before it can offer any three-dimensional shape at all.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.
